result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, **Linear is the best overall project management tool** if you're building a tech product. But the best choice depends on your team size, workflow, and whether you need product development, general project management, or company-wide operations.

My recommendation is to prioritize five things\:

1. **Simplicity** – your team should be able to start using it immediately.
2. **Low overhead** – managing work shouldn't become work itself.
3. **Visibility** – everyone should know what's being worked on and what's blocked.
4. **Scalability** – it should grow with your team.
5. **Integrations** – Slack, GitHub, Google Workspace, and other tools should connect easily.

## My top 6 startup project management tools

![Fast growing startups are built on Linear](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/piHpddRS6n9dTggcCRU3QzspXui7xfTg4qksC0xamyVTz0l5rmZLEYCGsVB7KKUouzfiOTbe-9ydzUq7UB2MFrNbZIGlaUSNjP0C8Bhd2CXnbxL2xZ05zw3USDTcATN8Ed4Fr3ygsGaA-sAB5VFRUeF1jd3BNolTylsoZGFQvpYkliFtHTL_AgaQh3gID9Z3?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Fast, clean interface.
- Great developer workflow and GitHub integration.
- Less suited to managing every business department.

[Visit Linear](https://linear.app/)

![ClickUp Review 2026: Honest In-Depth Analysis & Features](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/IhDLDOyxNDHrKHznRnMbzyjIK7Vr4N5HNf17bkJW7PnIqc3qMmYgJU2IqfzLiCBJatpbDtLiH4ToLtJwHlzGNnvDPQLGe5YS9YbILi94CXJmy4xFdhZmSjqz-lpCT9-ubZzBBG-nlRcQIsvn8DaSyQoEPl_3wXUG0qs9BW4SnIccpcG_XWfRoc5BRY_9ndY5?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one solution)

- Tasks, projects, documents and goals.
- Dashboards and automations.
- Suitable for product, marketing, operations and sales.
- Can become complicated if over-customized.

[Visit ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![Project Management Hub Template by Gridvio | Notion Marketplace](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6e1oG6Y_aW5V5yDl222hE8Y8t-T__05L0OPLqrtY2b6KrmvS_M-QH4eaVLv4afPJUAGCFGr_eoifL-Irt3_HiUqUmKW08dRjhIxW2MfVWL_nPAWNaujkMp5zdq2VbJkW7b3h6jvrTVNAFmmVU9MPLCBztqWrhslDc_LeRhpbcV451et11onvlpgBLkBnIYcR?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage startups)

- Project management and company wiki.
- Meeting notes, documentation and processes.
- Flexible databases and templates.
- Less powerful for complex project execution.

[Visit Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

![New: Asana’s Milestones help you visualize project progress • Asana](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/045PY8MNTZCNbuEY_9zoc2ZmyVm82bEUQrACKq4DMJ2rZRzBOKtwnHDDeSB865DF__R-b4CGI6GEhHdu4YJMzkB1qcjJuCRLXmMhkxG9zfIfGx-0L1EgDFt_aMUwOdh5HR45ijTcFpeq8HRM8juB5v_Vffpp7OzTfiaEKInBCXkUCm5590f5v87DKC8sKsga?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent cross-team coordination.
- Clear task ownership and deadlines.
- Strong project timelines and dependencies.
- Good for growing non-technical teams.

[Visit Asana](https://asana.com/)

---

![What's New - monday.com Product Updates](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/A6uqDbwZDZtLi6fdSQ4vBgCQbnekV0PIx4KVuVyvOr829LpE2bCzHdwMLqPfPl8gWESkzkwLYt7S32LGreo4ooKI7LMbOa3LDgEJY5XamBVn4I4fKACcjxheDQNjN3kYBWjEyVTME7rTaH0lrtDPHD2D7YT1KNXf7LC0zf16zSR-GU4N3mIXikR458xkW8a1?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Excellent visual dashboards.
- Useful for marketing, operations and sales.
- Powerful automation and reporting.
- Can get expensive as the team grows.

[Visit Monday.com](https://monday.com/)

---

![How to Toggle Trello Views: Calendar, Table, Timeline & More](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Md351UxojPqr7NcZARTUVuAl7ocTctX4xXxse2slXCoIC1a14ed7C82Suo3_BLOf8uMvPvkR6a7txy4RworeyrfELrkzyRnZeSU5JT9wx8ysI4A-zP3PbB-iwMrUJ8znrFR0rgAWlJ-HP1EFK6mtsJMgFbfykp-Rc-ETfrBKJfKEo5IF5n0UcFY7ie8JejkV?purpose=fullsize)

**6\. Trello**

- Very easy to learn.
- Simple Kanban boards.
- Good for small teams and limited budgets.
- Limited functionality for complex workflows.

[Visit Trello](https://trello.com/)

## Which would I choose?

| Startup situation | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| 2–5 founders, pre-seed | Notion |
| SaaS / technology startup | Linear + Notion |
| 5–20 employees, mixed teams | ClickUp |
| Marketing / agency startup | Asana |
| Scaling operations | Monday.com |
| Minimal budget | Trello |


**My overall recommendation\:** If you want one tool to manage the entire startup, start with ClickUp. If you're a technology startup, use Linear for product development and Notion for company knowledge.
